record_identity.title: Transparent composite usage-cost attribution and reset integrity

summary: Proposes a cross-domain Caelestis amendment package requiring finite AI usage allowances to remain economically legible where depletion is produced by variable model capability, reasoning effort, context processing, tools, connectors, delegated agents, background execution, retries, failed work, execution location, or shared-pool activity. The proposal also distinguishes reset, replenishment, rollover, expiry, compensatory credit, and authoritative entitlement restoration so that an aggregate percentage or remaining balance cannot substitute for meaningful usage-cost attribution.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: CAM already recognises utility-access systems, usage capacity, provisioning, depletion, expiry, rollover, restriction, fallback, remediation, proportional resource consumption, and account-state ambiguity. Modern agentic services nevertheless charge or deplete a composite resource whose principal drivers may be invisible to the affected user. Without attribution, users cannot predict consumption, compare modes of use, determine whether failed or retried work was charged, identify which surface consumed a shared pool, verify that a reset restored entitlement, or contest an unexplained depletion event. This is an economic-state provenance and runtime-integrity gap rather than a demand for unlimited access or disclosure of proprietary infrastructure.
evidence_confidence: corroborated architecture and complaint cluster; precise provider weighting formulas remain undisclosed

source_records.source_title: Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan
source_records.deployment_context: ChatGPT plans using Codex and related agentic surfaces.
source_records.source_context: OpenAI states that Codex usage counts toward an agentic usage limit, that multiple agentic surfaces may draw from the same usage structure, and that larger codebases, long-running tasks, and extended sessions requiring more context consume significantly more per message.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary evidence that contemporary usage depletion is variable, task-sensitive, and potentially shared across surfaces rather than reducible to a simple message count.

contextual_relations.note: Existing account-resource ambiguity remains relevant where users cannot determine which account, workspace, pool, reset, or entitlement governs depletion, but this proposal does not claim to repair FM-0007.
Existing access-state governance remains relevant to reset and entitlement restoration, but this proposal addresses economic attribution and reset integrity rather than all access-state failures.
Cross-client and cross-surface usage-state divergence is contextual evidence; this proposal does not collapse runtime non-equivalence into the Economics repair chain.

migration_notes: Individual records maintain canonical source evidence only in source_records. Do not add source_data or duplicate primary sources in linked_records.external_references.
proposal_rationale: Finite usage allowances are legitimate economic mechanisms when their scope, depletion, reset, and remediation states are sufficiently legible. The governance failure arises where users are shown only an aggregate balance while material consumption is produced by hidden combinations of model capability, reasoning effort, context, tools, agents, retries, failed execution, background work, execution location, and cross-surface pool sharing. The proposal therefore seeks a proportionate attribution duty rather than exact disclosure of proprietary infrastructure or a guarantee of unlimited access.

proposal_scope.scope_summary: Add Charter-level intelligible utility-access depletion, composite usage-cost attribution, shared-pool legibility, reset and entitlement integrity, failed-work charging provenance, material methodology-change disclosure, and downstream runtime handoff requirements.

suggested_insertion_points: ECONOMICS-001: add a Charter-level Intelligible Utility-Access Depletion principle beneath economic auditability and proportionality controls.
ECONOMICS-003: extend Usage Capacity semantics with composite usage-cost attribution, shared-pool legibility, reset-state distinctions, and failed-work depletion provenance.

ECONOMICS-003: extend semantic handoff fields with usage_pool_id, usage_surface, model_or_capability_tier, reasoning_effort, foreground_usage, background_usage, tool_usage, delegated_agent_usage, retry_usage, failed_execution_usage, context_processing_usage, shared_pool_contribution, reset_event_type, reset_effective_state, depletion_attribution_status, and remediation_eligibility.
OPERATIONS-001-SUP-01: require runtime receipts that preserve the principal usage drivers without requiring disclosure of proprietary internal architecture.
AEON-008-SCH-01: consume economic signals for depletion, reset, remediation, contested state, and protective fallback where applicable.
AEON-003-SCH-04: arbitrate unresolved authoritative account, workspace, pool, entitlement, reset, or cross-client state.
schema_changes: Possible addition of controlled reset-state and depletion-attribution fields to Economics semantic handoff schemas.
validator_changes: Possible consistency checks if new fields or controlled values are registered across multiple instruments.
automation_changes: Rebuild governance indexes and verify cross-document section references after corpus adoption.
interface_changes: Expose principal depletion drivers, shared-pool contribution, reset state, failed-work attribution, and remediation eligibility in a user-accessible receipt or explanation surface.
migration_concerns: Do not imply retrospective entitlement to exact historic task-level receipts where the provider did not preserve the required telemetry.
Do not collapse pricing disclosure, usage attribution, account entitlement, and runtime execution state into one undifferentiated field.
Do not require publication of security-sensitive or proprietary implementation details where categorical attribution is sufficient for user understanding and contestability.
dependencies: Full Caelestis source-authority and cross-reference review
Decision on whether new ECON.RC, ECON.MECH, or ECON.HARM controlled values are required
Human review of proportionality and commercial-confidentiality boundaries

external_relevance.external_summary: The proposal is relevant wherever AI access is sold or provisioned through finite, weighted, pooled, or resettable usage capacity. It offers a governance basis for consumer and enterprise transparency without prescribing prices, unlimited access, or disclosure of proprietary infrastructure.

next_action: Perform a full Caelestis Economics-domain and Annex G source-authority review, confirm exact insertion points and non-duplicative wording, decide whether a distinct opaque composite usage-depletion failure mode is needed, and draft the minimal cross-domain amendment package for human governance review.
